risk_register.description: If SSO provider identity, sandbox access, or API documentation is not confirmed before Phase 2 begins, then authentication integration cannot proceed, blocking UC1 (Authenticate User) and all dependent use cases (UC2, UC3, UC5, UC6). Development team cannot validate SSO integration until late Phase 2, causing 2–4 week timeline slip and potential re-architecture if provider does not support required grant flows.
risk_register.trigger: Open Question #1 remains unanswered at Phase 2 kickoff; SSO provider sandbox not accessible to development team by end of week 1
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm SSO provider identity and request sandbox/test environment access immediately (week 0); validate API documentation completeness and required grant flows (OAuth 2.0, SAML, etc.) before Phase 2 sprint planning; assign Backend Developer to SSO integration spike in Phase 1 to de-risk provider compatibility
risk_register.contingency: If SSO provider sandbox is unavailable, establish direct escalation path to SSO vendor support; prepare alternative authentication approach (temporary API key or test account) to unblock Phase 2 development; if provider does not support required flows, evaluate alternative SSO provider (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) and re-estimate integration effort

risk_register.description: If email service (SMTP, SendGrid, AWS SES) is not provisioned and accessible before Phase 2 begins, then UC5 (Schedule Report Delivery) cannot be implemented on schedule. Procurement and integration of a new email service requires 1–2 weeks; if existing service has delivery SLA < 99%, success metric '90% of scheduled reports delivered on time' becomes unachievable without service swap or metric re-negotiation.
risk_register.trigger: Open Question #2 remains unanswered at Phase 2 kickoff; email service not provisioned or SLA < 99% confirmed by end of week 1
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm email service availability and SLA (target ≥ 99%) immediately (week 0); if not provisioned, evaluate and procure service (SendGrid, AWS SES, or internal SMTP) before Phase 2 sprint planning; validate email delivery rate and latency in test environment; document email service API and rate limits for backend integration
risk_register.contingency: If email service is unavailable, procure alternative service and integrate in Phase 2 (adds 1–2 weeks); if SLA is < 99%, re-negotiate success metric '90% on-time delivery' with stakeholders or implement retry/fallback logic to improve delivery reliability

risk_register.description: If PagerDuty integration scope is not explicitly defined (threshold-based alerts only vs. custom escalation policies, on-call schedule management, incident lifecycle automation), then backend development effort could increase 40–60% if stakeholders expect advanced workflows. Scope ambiguity discovered mid-Phase 2 causes rework, backlog re-prioritization, and timeline slip of 1–2 weeks.
risk_register.trigger: Open Question #3 remains unanswered at Phase 2 kickoff; stakeholder feedback during Phase 2 sprint review reveals expectation of custom escalation policies or incident automation not in original scope
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm PagerDuty integration scope explicitly in Phase 1 (week 0–1): threshold-based alert triggering (UC6, UC7) only, no custom escalation policies or on-call automation; document scope boundary in acceptance criteria for T13, T14, T15, T18, T21; obtain written stakeholder sign-off on PagerDuty scope before Phase 2 sprint planning
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholders request custom escalation policies or incident automation mid-Phase 2, evaluate effort (40–60% increase) and present timeline/budget trade-off to leadership; prioritize threshold-based alerts (MVP) and defer advanced workflows to Phase 4 or post-launch backlog

risk_register.description: If Product Manager is unavailable or not actively engaged during Phase 2–3 sprint cycles, then backlog prioritization, sprint planning, and stakeholder feedback loops will be delayed. Hybrid SDLC requires active PO engagement for adaptive sprint cycles; undefined or part-time PO role causes decision delays, sprint planning friction, and scope creep.
risk_register.trigger: Open Question #4 remains unanswered at Phase 2 kickoff; Product Manager unavailable for sprint planning, daily standups, or sprint reviews during Phase 2–3; competing priorities documented for PM role
risk_register.mitigation: Confirm Product Manager is dedicated (100% allocation) to this project for Phases 2–3 (weeks 3–12); establish sprint cadence (2-week sprints) with fixed sprint planning, daily standup, and sprint review times; assign PM as single decision-maker for scope changes and backlog prioritization; document PM availability and escalation path for urgent decisions
risk_register.contingency: If PM becomes unavailable mid-project, designate backup decision-maker (e.g., Customer Success Team lead or Sales leader) with authority to approve scope changes and prioritize backlog; establish asynchronous decision-making process (Slack, email) for non-urgent decisions to minimize sprint planning delays

risk_register.description: If the existing customer analytics dashboard codebase has unknown technical debt, low test coverage, or architectural constraints not visible in the brief, then Phase 1 discovery could reveal integration complexity or refactoring needs that compress Phase 2 timeline. Unknown codebase state could add 1–2 weeks of unplanned work.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 codebase review (T1, T2, T3) reveals test coverage < 50%, significant technical debt, or architectural constraints that affect real-time reporting or alerting integration; refactoring effort estimated > 5 days
risk_register.mitigation: Conduct comprehensive codebase health assessment in Phase 1 (T1, T2): measure test coverage, identify technical debt, document architectural constraints affecting real-time data refresh, alerting, and email scheduling; prioritize refactoring work before Phase 2 feature development; allocate 2–3 days in Phase 1 for critical refactoring if needed
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 1 reveals significant technical debt (> 1 week refactoring), re-negotiate Phase 2 scope with stakeholders: defer non-critical features (e.g., custom report filters) to Phase 4 or post-launch; compress Phase 2 timeline by reducing feature scope or extending deadline by 1–2 weeks

risk_register.description: If any critical path task (T1, T2, T3, T6, T11, T16, T21, T26) slips by more than 1 day, then the entire project timeline compresses, reducing buffer for Phase 3 UAT and Phase 4 deployment. 12-week deadline with 4-person team and zero slack on critical path leaves no margin for integration issues, external dependency delays, or rework.
risk_register.trigger: Any critical path task (T1, T2, T3, T6, T11, T16, T21, T26) slips by > 1 day; external dependency (SSO provider, email service, PagerDuty) delivery delayed; Phase 2 sprint review reveals integration rework needed
risk_register.mitigation: Establish daily standup discipline for critical path tasks; assign Backend Developer and Product Manager as dedicated (not shared) resources for Phases 1–4; implement risk-driven sprint planning: prioritize de-risking SSO, email, and PagerDuty integrations in Phase 2 weeks 1–2; maintain 2–3 day buffer in Phase 3 for UAT rework
risk_register.contingency: If critical path task slips > 1 day, immediately escalate to Product Manager and leadership; evaluate scope reduction (defer Phase 4 features to post-launch) or timeline extension (push deadline to 2025-04-24); activate contingency resources (contractor backend developer) if slip exceeds 2 days

risk_register.description: If data retention policy (2 years) is not implemented in the database schema and data lifecycle management, then the system may violate internal compliance requirements or create unplanned operational overhead. Data retention enforcement is not explicitly mapped to a use case or task; implementation details are undefined.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 requirements review reveals data retention policy is not implemented in current dashboard; Phase 2 backend development does not include data lifecycle management (archival, deletion) tasks; Phase 3 UAT discovers compliance gap
risk_register.mitigation: Define data retention implementation approach in Phase 1 (T2, T3): database schema design for data archival/deletion, scheduled job for data lifecycle management, audit logging for compliance; assign Backend Developer to implement data retention in Phase 2 (add 2–3 days to T11 or T16); validate data retention enforcement in Phase 3 UAT
risk_register.contingency: If data retention is not implemented by Phase 3 UAT, defer to post-launch backlog and implement in Phase 4 or as operational task; document compliance risk and obtain stakeholder acceptance of deferred implementation
